meta.title: Soap in the Stream
meta.textType: story: the theme and the parts

paragraphs: On Thursday, Teacher Kim told the Explorers about a big event. "On Saturday, we will help Ranger Mark at the campsite in the nature park," she said. "We will clean the campsite, and we will work in teams." Lily, Mia, Leo, and May were in the same team. "Will Ranger Mark show us the stream?" asked Mia. "Yes, he will," said Teacher Kim.

On Saturday morning, Ranger Mark met the children at the gate of the campsite. He wore a green cap and brown boots. Everyone had a hat and a bag. The team went to the wash house first. Lily picked up paper and plastic bottles near the sink. Leo counted the bags. May wrote the numbers on a list. Soon they had ten full bags.

Then Mia called, "Come and look!" The stream was white with soap, and it smelled sweet. A bottle of soap lay on a stone next to the water. "Some visitors washed their plates here," said May. "But why is that a problem?" asked Leo. Ranger Mark came quickly and looked at the water. "Soap looks clean, but it is not good for a stream," he said. "If soap goes into the water, the small fish will be ill."

"What can we do?" asked Lily. "First, take the bottle away," said Ranger Mark. Lily put the bottle in her bag. Then the team filled two buckets with clean water from the wash house. They put it into the stream. Slowly, the soap went away. "Visitors can wash plates at the sink," said Ranger Mark. "Being a ranger is my career, and I have worked here for twelve years." "I look after this stream every day." Lily looked at the clear water and smiled.

In the evening, Lily wrote a post for Explorers' Blog. The title was "Clean Park, Clean Stream". Mia put in a photo of the clear water. Leo drew a small fish. Teacher Kim read the post, and she gave it a big smile. "Now many people will know about the stream," she said. A small thing at the sink can help a whole stream.
